name: Push-up
pattern: Horizontal push: the body stays one straight plank while the arms bend and straighten.
setup: Hands under your shoulders, a little wider, fingers forward.
Legs straight, feet together or hip width, on your toes.
Squeeze your glutes and brace: head, hips and heels in one line.

steps.text: Bend your elbows and lower your chest between your hands, elbows about 45° from your sides.
Stop with your chest a fist's height from the floor.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight, the body rising as one piece.
At the top, keep pushing so your shoulder blades spread around your ribs.

cues.cue: One straight line from head to heels.
cues.why: The abdominals give most of the stiffness that stops the lower back sagging.
Hands turned in or placed forward raise the load on the elbow.

cues.cue: About 45° from your sides, like an arrow, not a T.
cues.why: Arms above about 60° from the body limit how the shoulder blade can rotate and tilt.

cues.cue: Chest to a fist's height from the floor.
cues.why: Full range trains the whole movement; most test standards ask for a 90° elbow.

cues.cue: Push the floor away at the top, shoulders away from your ears.
cues.why: The push-up plus trains the serratus anterior and lowers upper-trapezius dominance.

breathing: Breathe in on the way down, out as you push up.

tempo.note: Lower for about 2 seconds, press in 1 to 2.

mistakes.name: Hips sag
mistakes.looks: The lower back arches and the hips drop below the line.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes, ribs down, body like a plank.
mistakes.why: The trunk muscles are not holding the spine; regress to an incline until you can hold the line.

mistakes.name: Elbows flare out
mistakes.looks: Upper arms point straight out to the sides, like a T.
mistakes.why: Wide elbows move the load onto the front of the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Head drops
mistakes.looks: The head hangs and the chin reaches for the floor first.
mistakes.fix: Look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
mistakes.why: It breaks the straight line and lets the shoulders round.

safety: Shoulder pain: keep elbows tucked below 60° and shorten the range.
Wrist pain: use fists or handles to keep the wrist straight; muscle activity stays the same.
Elbow pain: avoid turning the hands in and very narrow hands.

variants.change: Hands raised: about 41% body weight at 61 cm, 55% at 30 cm. Same arm keyframes, body tilted to the bench angle.
Feet raised: about 70-74% body weight; more upper chest and front delt.
Hands narrow: more triceps and more load on the elbow.
Hands wide: more chest, more load moves to the shoulder.

subtypes.name: Knee push-up
subtypes.change: Knees on the floor about 90°, hips straight, same arms.

subtypes.name: Incline push-up
subtypes.change: Whole body tilted up to the bench or wall, same arms.

subtypes.name: Pike push-up
subtypes.change: Hips high, trunk near vertical, head goes toward the floor: an overhead press pattern.

motion.basis: Elbow flexion, elbow flare and scapular angles from suprak2013 and lunden2010; trunk (90 = horizontal, here 75-86 because the hands are higher than the feet) and shoulder flexion estimated from the body line. Baked rig: Body/anatomy/rig_za.py.
